 Katie & Nathaniel — Behind the Scenes  2005-10-15

Story Crossroads Dossier: Virginia Domicile, Touring Warwick University on Route 112 NNTC, & Keeping Wesley, Katie's Career, and Both Rescues

How Staying in Virginia on In-State Tuition Domicile Lets Heather Drive Nate, Katie, and Wesley to Warwick University, Eliminates Tiffany, Stops Brandon Cold, and Preserves Katie's Senate Career and Both Cousin Rescues

Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4: Story Crossroads Outside the Virginia Beach Pavilion ↗ Katie & Nathaniel (25 Dossiers) Copy Link: Read on Phone

Scan with your camera to continue reading this dossier on your phone or tablet.
Story Date & Time 2005-10-15 • 13:15 EDT
Setting Virginia Beach, Norfolk, & Newport News, Virginia (Northwood High School, CCHR, Virginia Dominion University, Warwick University, & Richmond)
Archival Source RaggieSoft Backstage Production Dossier
Addressed To Readers of Katie & Nathaniel (Episode 4, Chapter 2 Story Crossroads)

Archival Note: In our earlier Minnesota Marriage 'What If' Dossier, Katie and Nathaniel Prairie relocating thirteen hundred miles north to Minnesota to be with Heather and Wesley spared the twins from Brandon and Tiffany—at the devastating cost of erasing Katie's Virginia political career and leaving Cousin Brittany and Cousin Chelsea unrescued.

That raised an essential question—especially for Wesley's sake, since sixteen-year-old Wesley never deserved to lose his very first guy friend through zero fault of his own—and directly inspired the coequal Story Crossroads at the conclusion of Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4: How does a Virginia timeline unfold when Nate and Katie welcome Heather back romantically (or when Cousin Hannah's green-parka lie happens first so trust is never broken), Heather and Wesley stay in Virginia on in-state college domicile, Katie still becomes a United States Senator, and both Brittany and Chelsea are rescued?

1. Two Coequal Ways Into the Virginia Domicile Timeline (Homeroom 212 or The Pavilion Crossroads)

Whether trust is preserved before New Year's Day or mended outside the Virginia Beach Pavilion on graduation morning, the structural foundation is identical:

  1. The Homeroom 212 Variant (December 2002 $\rightarrow$ Monday, January 6, 2003):
    If Kristen Bauer's varsity-table takedown of Tyler's "mystery redhead behind the Kempsville Plaza movie theater" lie about Gavin Whitfield's cousin Hannah happens right before Winter Break instead of February, seventeen-year-old Heather Collins hears Tyler's sleazebag script three weeks before he tries it on her. When Tyler leans over her desk in Homeroom 212 on January 6 claiming Nate locked a bedroom door with "some pretty blonde girl," Heather calls him an idiot ("That was his twin sister Katie!")—and when Tyler doubles down claiming it was someone else, Heather laughs right in his face because across eighteen months the only girls Nate has ever spent time with are Katie, Heather, and earlier Cousin Brittany (leaving Heather wondering why Brittany threw a party when the twins hate alcohol rather than doubting Nate for a second). Publicly torched, Tyler still retreats to Smoker's Corner on Macgregory Street that spring and still traps shunned Brittany onto a South Richmond lease by 2013.
  2. The Live Story Crossroads Path (Saturday, June 14, 2003 at the Virginia Beach Pavilion):
    At the interactive Story Crossroads at the end of Episode 4, Chapter 2, Part 4, when sixteen-year-old Wesley holds his breath turning his smooth blue silicone ring between both palms after Heather confesses the whole truth, choosing Accept Heather's Apology & Welcome Her Back lets Katie and Nate forgive Heather under the blooming crape-myrtles—turning Pomp and Circumstance into the moment Wesley throws his fist into the air cheering instead of crying.

2. Staying in Virginia Under Code of Virginia § 23-7.4 & Mutual Package-Deal Devotion

Once Nate and Heather are together in June 2003, eighteen-year-old Heather sits down at the kitchen table with her parents, Aunt Linda, and David Prairie with a rock-solid financial and legal reality under Code of Virginia § 23-7.4 (Virginia's one-year continuous college domicile statute):

  • Why Leaving Virginia Costs Thousands:
    Having lived continuously in Hampton Roads throughout high school, Heather already holds full Virginia in-state tuition domicile for the Community College of Hampton Roads (CCHR) 2+2 Guaranteed Transfer pathway and Virginia Dominion University (VDU) in Norfolk—whereas uprooting to bounce between states forfeits Virginia domicile and breaks sixteen-year-old Wesley's established Tidewater routines and developmental-services continuity.
  • Mutual Package-Deal Devotion (Two Pairs = One Household of Four):
    When Aunt Linda stays in Tidewater for one transitional year before her July 2004 medical crisis—at which point nineteen-year-old Heather petitions the Virginia Circuit Court to become eighteen-year-old Wesley's plenary legal guardian and conservator—all four adults live by a mutual, unbreakable covenant:
  • Heather respects with her whole heart: Wherever Nate goes, Katie goes too.
  • Nate and Katie respect with their whole hearts: Wherever Heather goes, Wesley goes too.

Instead of Katie and Nate renting a tiny studio alone on Greenway Court, Nate, Katie, Heather, and Wesley move into a zero-step ground-floor three-bedroom Norfolk/Kempsville apartment right along CVTA Routes #2 and #15, with David Prairie building rolling kitchen carts and wide desk bays for all four of them.

3. 2004–2005: Eliminating Tiffany, Stopping Brandon Cold, & Touring Warwick University Beside 112 NNTC

Living together as an unbroken four-person household transforms Katie and Nate's early twenties while preserving every geographical detail of their Tidewater canon:

  1. Tiffany Sloan Is 100% Eliminated:
    Because Nate stays happily loyal to Heather (studying side by side at CCHR and VDU before marrying Heather in a barrier-free Kempsville ceremony), Nate never dates Tiffany Sloan in November 2004.
  2. Brandon Mercer Hits a Four-Person Brick Wall (May 2004):
    The very first afternoon Brandon Mercer visits their Norfolk apartment after meeting Katie at CCHR and tries to talk condescendingly over seventeen-year-old Wesley or suggest Katie come up to Williamsburg "just the two of us without your brother," Heather calls out every controlling red flag to his face in thirty seconds flat—while six-foot-tall Wesley steps squarely in front of Nate's and Katie's footrests, folds both arms across his chest over his blue silicone ring, and fixes Brandon with an unmovable sentinel glare until Brandon backs out the front door for good. Zero Williamsburg captivity, zero Ocean View isolation, and zero thirteen years sleeping on closet floors.
  3. Summer 2003 (Ten-Campus College Tour Between Wesley's Sophomore & Junior Years — Including Warwick University Beside 112 NNTC, Shenandoah Valley University [SVU], RRC Redmond Hall, CPI, & North Star State University in Minnesota):
    Right between sixteen-year-old Wesley's sophomore and junior years of high school—so that once Wesley graduates two years later, he will already know where he wants to go with zero deadline pressure—Heather and Aunt Linda organize a ten-campus tour (July–August 2003):
    • Stops 1–4 (Tidewater & Peninsula): CCHR Norfolk -> Virginia Dominion University (VDU, Hampton Blvd, watching 2NAVAL STATIONvia HAMPTON BLVD glide past) -> Warwick University (WU, Newport News — Heather drives across the HRBT preserving Katie & Nate's zero Peninsula-route knowledge, spotting 112 NNTC at the SR-312 & Shoe Lane roundabout) -> College of Charles & Anne (C&A, Williamsburg — uneven 18th-century brick walkways rattling Katie's & Nate's front casters).
    • Stops 5–7 (Richmond, Fairfax, & Harrisonburg): Central Virginia University (CVU, West Broad Street sirens) -> George Wythe University (GWU, four-hour I-95 crawl from Tidewater) -> Shenandoah Valley University (SVU, Harrisonburg — in-universe James Madison University), where a loud Summer Preview Open House pep band and purple-and-gold balloon arch overwhelm sixteen-year-old Wesley so the tour is cut short, though Wesley signals he would be interested in checking SVU out again when it isn't an Open House.
    • Stops 8–9 (Fishersville & Blacksburg): Driving 35 minutes south on I-81 from Harrisonburg to Roosevelt Rehabilitation Center (RRC) in Fishersville, the four check in at the Bates-Harding reception window—and because Redmond Hall (the medical dormitory) is attached inside that exact administration building, the tour stops short sixty yards from check-in the moment the guide explains gender-separated dorms and mandatory Redmond Hall placement. Knowing that whenever Wesley wakes up scared and crying at night, he instinctively climbs into bed with his Safe Person, Heather, to be cuddled until he calms down, sixteen-year-old Wesley cries his eyes out in Heather's arms, and Heather politely tells the tour guide that this is Wesley making his decision, and that the answer is no. That afternoon at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in Blacksburg, Nate falls in love with the mountain valley and Ironstone quad, yet worries that Blacksburg's steep hills will drain their 24-volt wheelchair batteries too fast.
    • Stop 10 (August 2003 Minnesota Family Visit & NSSU Tour): Katie and Nate fly north with Heather, Aunt Linda, and Wesley to meet Heather and Wesley's extended family outside Saint Paul and ride the intercampus bus at North Star State University (NSSU) before returning home to Tidewater.

4. 2007–2029+: Heather's Special Education Career, Katie's Political Rise, & Rescuing Both Brittany and Chelsea

Because Heather never moves to Minnesota and never meets wildlife biologist Dan Lindstrom, North Lion Scales & Tails never opens in this timeline—and every milestone of Heather's own Special Education calling, Katie Prairie's public-service career, and both cousin rescues unfolds organically:

  • Heather's Special Education Teaching Career + Prairie Twin Interactive:
    While Katie and Nate launch Prairie Twin Interactive, LLC, Heather (VDU Special Education — Adapted Curriculum) begins her career as a dedicated Special Education teacher in Hampton Roads—living out their mirrored household promise (wherever Nate goes, Katie goes too; wherever Heather goes, Wesley goes with her).
  • Katie's Political Rise (2010–2026):
    Even though Heather drives an accessible van when the four-person household travels across the harbor together, Katie and Nate proudly ride Southside CVTA public buses every day for their own daily independence. Katie still hits Virginia Beach's 5:30 PM Municipal Center bus curfew, still wins Kempsville City Council (2010) and the 85th House District (2013), and still defeats House Bill 663 on Thursday, February 4, 2016 alongside Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins and Uncle Richard Callaway.
  • February 6, 2016 & July 2016 (Rescuing Both Brittany and Chelsea):
    On Saturday, February 6, 2016, Nate, Katie, and Heather walk and roll into that South Richmond church together—all three Northwood Class of 2003 alumni facing down Tyler as Nate says "I object!" to bring Brittany safely home to Kempsville. Five months later, David, Katie, Nate, Heather, and Brittany bring thirty-four-year-old Cousin Chelsea (hugging her green plush Shelly Turtle) home from Braxton, Rhode Island—where twenty-nine-year-old Wesley is already waiting on Arvin Road to welcome her, giving Wesley and Chelsea twelve extra years side by side in Virginia Beach before U.S. Senator Katie Prairie passes the landmark 2028 Supported Companions Act!

5. Comparing Both Coequal Pavilion Story Paths

(Note: A hypothetical "total refusal" option—where Katie and Nate roll away from the Pavilion without even granting Wesley a farewell Saturday—is intentionally absent because neither Nate nor Katie could ever break sixteen-year-old Wesley's heart when he did nothing wrong.)
